info.title: UsableNet AQA - API v3.1
info.description:
This environment lets you check specifications for UsableNet AQA API v3.1. In order to test API v3.1 you'll need to provide: 1. your team's *slug*, as `teamSlug` server variable; 2. your associated API key, as authorization token to be passed as `"X-Team"` HTTP header value. You can retrieve both by accessing your AQA profile page ("API Keys & Views" section). If you have troubles retrieving this information contact your IT or human resources department. --- # General API specifications All API paths are relative to the server URL `api-aqa.usablenet.com`, and share the same base path `/{apiversion}/{teamslug}/{apipath}`. All API return `"application/json"` as response content type. All calls are stateless, therefore no cookies are returned nor necessary. As said, authorization is managed via `"X-Team"` custom HTTP header. Optionally, pretty-printing of API response body can be enabled by adding a custom HTTP request header named `"X-API-Response-Format"` with value `"prettyPrint"`. ## API error responses All API responses with a status code different from `200` comply with this structure: ```json { "statusCode": {statuscode}, "error": "{error_key}" } ``` High-level errors, applying to all APIs, may include the following: | Status code | Error key | Reason | |-------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `401` | `"unauthorized"` | Invalid team *slug* or invalid API key | | `403` | `"pending_agreement"` | Authorized user (being API key valid) must first accept UsableNet AQA SaaS User Agreement | | `405` | `"method_not_allowed"` | Unsupported request method | | `501` | `"api_not_supported"` | Unsupported or unrecognized API, e.g. due to typos in its path | --- # Release notes ## API v3.1.0 *New features:* - support for *ruleset packages*, for *accessibility tests*; as *rulesets* evolve, new *packages* will be introduced. - when inspecting *accessibility tests* or *accessibility test runs*, *package* is also returned (visiting `ruleset.pack`). *Breaking changes*: - `/v3.1/{teamslug}//a11y/tests/rulesets` returns *rulesets* grouped by *ruleset package*; - when creating an *accessibility test*, a *ruleset package* must be specified; - when inspecting the *flow/page* issues of a *test run* and evaluating an HTML web page, in the vocabulary of extensive descriptions of the issues detected automatically by AQA, `descriptions[issue.ruleId][issue.solutionId].solution` was replaced with an expanded list of `solutions`, each presented with a title and text description, in HTML format. ## API v3.0.2 *New features:* - for *accessibility tests* and *keyboard navigation tests*: - scheduler configuration settings: added "Once every 3 months" option; - data retention (formerly "trashing behaviour"): added "last 30 runs" aside time-based policies; older *runs* are automatically moved to *Trashed runs* once the limit is reached. ## API v3.0.1 *New features:* - when inspecting *flow*/*page* issues of an *accessibility test* *run*, user comments can be optionally included. ## API v3.0.0 AQA API v3 embraces the workflows, content organization and terminology introduced with AQA 2024, while also expanding supported features and bringing a few changes to improve ease of use and readability. *New features:* - for *flows* and *crawlers*: - when creating a *flow* or *crawler*, support for configurations where another *flow* is selected as reference to inherit settings or continue from it; - deletion of *flows* and *crawlers*; - *accessibility tests* and *keyboard navigation tests* seamlessly integrated with AQA experience, with support for scheduling, notifications and automatic reports generation; - user management features: AQA user accounts can be created, edited or deleted via API, as well as their team memberships; - POST requests support both `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `application/json` content types. *Breaking changes:* - content created via API v2.x is not compatible with API v3; when available, is presented on AQA in dedicated sections (named "Accessibility tests via API v2" and "Keyboard navigation tests via API v2" respectively). > To retrieve *accessibility tests* and *keyboard navigation tests* created via API v2.x and their results, you must use API v2.x. - updated specs for POST requests: - the names of all parameters and request body keys changed from lowercase (e.g. `"deviceid"`, `"collectmaxtime"`) to camel case (`"deviceId"`, `"collectMaxTime"`) to improve readability; - when creating *accessibility tests* and *keyboard navigation tests*, implicit inclusion of all compatible *flows*/*crawlers* (`partid` param not specified) is not allowed anymore; - for additional breaking changes specific to each API check out Upgrading from API v2 chapter. ### Upgrading from API v2 The following table illustrates how to upgrade API v2.x to API v3. > API paths are taken from API v2.2; if you're using previous API versions, we recommend upgrading to API v2.2 first. | API v2.2 | API v3 | |-----|-----| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites`

*Breaking changes (API request):*
  • `parttype` query param replaced by the combination of `flowType` and `crawlerType` query params
*Breaking changes (API response):*
  • renamed:
    • `projects` → `suites`
      For each element in the list:
      • `numParts` replaced by the combination of `numFlows` and `numCrawlers`
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects/{projectid}` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}`

*Breaking changes (API request):*
  • `parttype` query param replaced by the combination of `flowType` and `crawlerType` query params
*Breaking changes (API response):*
  • `numParts` replaced by the combination of `numFlows` and `numCrawlers`
  • `parts` replaced by the combination of `flows` and `crawlers`
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects/{projectid}/{partid}` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/flows/{flowId}`
or
`/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/crawlers/{crawlerId}`
depending on whether it's a *flow* or *crawler* | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects/{projectid}/functional/create` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/flows/url/create`

*Breaking changes (API request):*
  • parameters' name changed from lowercase to camel case
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects/{projectid}/functional/{partid}/update` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/flows/{flowId}/update`

*Breaking changes (API request):*
  • parameters' name changed from lowercase to camel case
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects/{projectid}/crawler/create` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/crawlers/url/create`

*Breaking changes (API request):*
  • parameters' name changed from lowercase to camel case
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/projects/{projectid}/crawler/{partid}/update` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/crawlers/{crawlerId}/update`

*Breaking changes (API request):*
  • parameters' name changed from lowercase to camel case
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/tests` | No equivalent API v3.

`/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests` returns a different set of *accessibility tests*. | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/create` | No equivalent API v3.

The same result can be achieved by creating a *run* of a given *accessibility test* (possibly creating it first):
  1. create *accessibilty test*:
    `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/create`
    Note: implicit inclusion of all compatible *flows*/*crawlers* is not allowed anymore. At least one *flow* ID or *crawler* ID must be selected.
  2. create *run*
    `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/{testId}/run`
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/{testid}/{partid}` | No equivalent API v3.

Use `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}` to retrieve the status and result summary of a given *accessibility test run*, or the list of its *flows* and *crawlers* via `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}/flows` and `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}/crawlers` respectively. | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/{testid}/{partid}/issues` | No equivalent API v3.

Use `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}/flows/{flowId}` or `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}/pages/{pageId}` to retrieve the extensive results and review for a given *flow* or *page* (respectively) of an *accessibility test run*.
For additional insight, use `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}/flows/{flowId}/issues` or `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/runs/{runId}/pages/{pageId}/issues` to get the list of their respective issues. | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/verifications` | No equivalent API v3.

`/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests` returns a different set of *keyboard navigation tests*. | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/verifications/create` | No equivalent API v3.

The same result can be achieved by creating a *run* of a given *keyboard navigation test* (possibly creating it first):
  1. create *keyboard navigation test*:
    `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests/create`
    Note: implicit inclusion of all compatible *flows* is not allowed anymore. At least one *flow* ID must be selected.
  2. create *run*
    `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests/{testId}/run`
| | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/verifications/{testid}/{partid}` | No equivalent API v3.

Use `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests/runs/{runId}` to retrieve the status and result summary of a given *keyboard navigation test run*, or the list of its *flows* via `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests/runs/{runId}/flows`. | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/verifications/{testid}/{partid}/issues` | No equivalent API v3.

Use `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests/runs/{runId}/flows/{flowId}` to retrieve the extensive results and review for a given *flow* of a *keyboard navigation test run*.
For additional insight, use `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/keyboardTests/runs/{runId}/flows/{flowId}/issues` to get the list of issues. | | `/v2.2/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/evaluate` | `/v3/{teamslug}/a11y/tests/evaluate`

post.description:
Creates a single page user flow, according to the given source type:
- `"url"` = creates a single-page user flow by defining a starting URL and manual settings,
- `"settings"` = creates a single-page user flow by defining a starting URL and inheriting settings from another *flow*,
- `"flow"` = creates a single-page user flow by continuing another *flow*.

Single-page user flows may be seen as a one-step user flow (`"functional"` *flow* type).

Returned error keys:
- `existing_name` - Duplicated name 
- `invalid_connection_settings` - Connection settings definition does not comply with the JSON schema specifications, or JSON object is not well-formed 
- `invalid_device_screen_index` - Invalid device screen index 
- `invalid_name` - Invalid name
- `invalid_url` - Invalid starting URL

post.description:
Update configuration settings of a user flow (`"functional"` type). Null values in request body are discarded and don't contribute to updating user flow settings.
Existing limitations on parameters are related to user flow's origin, as returned by `/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/{partId}` API (visiting `data.origin` path, in dot notation). They apply to:
  • `url`: starting URL cannot be updated when flow recording starts from hosted content or continues from another *flow*;
  • `deviceId`, `deviceScreenIndex`, `connectionSettings`: device settings and connection settings cannot be updated if they're inherited from another *flow* (`data.origin.chainType` is defined and non-null).

400.description: Unsupported *flow* configuration, invalid value for *flow* configuration, or duplicated name

origin_not_supported.summary: Configuration updates incompatible with recording type
origin_not_supported.description: Configuration settings cannot be updated due to *flow*'s recording type: starting URL cannot be updated when recording starts from hosted content or continues from another *flow*

chain_type_not_supported.summary: Configuration updates incompatible with chain type
chain_type_not_supported.description: Configuration settings cannot be updated as they're inherited from another *flow*: it applies to device, device screen and connection settings

invalid_connection_settings.description: Connection settings definition does not comply with the JSON schema specifications, or JSON object is not well-formed

post.description:
Delete a user flow (`"functional"` type).  
A user flow referenced by other *flows*/*crawlers* as source (to inherit settings or continue from it) cannot be deleted.

Update configuration settings of a *crawler* (`"crawler"` type). Null values in request body are discarded and don't contribute to updating page collection settings.
Existing limitations on parameters are related to page collection's origin, as returned by `/a11y/suites/{suiteId}/{partId}` API (visiting `data.origin` path, in dot notation). They apply to:

  • `deviceId`, `deviceScreenIndex`: device settings cannot be updated if they're inherited from another *flow* (`data.origin.chainType` is defined and non-null).

issues.description:
The custom dropdown is not fully accessible.
The ROLE and ARIA attributes are not correctly set.

Follow the w3c instructions to create accessible custom dropdowns:
https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices-1.2/examples/listbox/listbox-collapsible.html
https://www.w3.org/TR/2019/NOTE-wai-aria-practices-1.1-20190814/examples/combobox/aria1.1pattern/listbox-combo.html

In some elements of this page (e.g the SEND MESSAGE button) the background color changes on focus event, and the text becomes invisible.
Ensure a contrast ratio of 4.5:1 also on focus event.

color_in_controls.problem: Some links or controls in the page that are identifiable by color (hue) are not visually identifiable via some other means (e.g., underlined, bolded, italicized, sufficient difference in lightness, etc).
color_in_controls.solution: • Check that any text where color is used to convey information is also styled or uses a font that makes it visually distinct from other text around it.

color_in_text.problem: Some text contents in the page use color as the only way to convey information.
color_in_text.solution: • Check that any text where color is used to convey information is also styled or uses a font that makes it visually distinct from other text around it.

input_missing_label.solution:
• Provide descriptive labels for any interactive component within Web content makes the component's purpose clear.
  • Use label elements to associate text labels with form controls. A label is attached to a specific form control through the use of the for attribute. The value of the for attribute must be the same as the value of the id attribute of the form control. The id attribute may have the same value as the name attribute, but both must be provided, and the id must be unique in the Web page.
  • Use WAI-ARIA attributes such as aria-label or aria-labelledby to provide descriptive label without using the label entity.

https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices-1.2/examples/listbox/listbox-collapsible.html
https://www.w3.org/TR/2019/NOTE-wai-aria-practices-1.1-20190814/examples/combobox/aria1.1pattern/listbox-combo.html

In some elements of this page (e.g the SEND MESSAGE button) the background color changes on focus event, and the text becomes invisible.
Ensure a contrast ratio of 4.5:1 also on focus event.

color_in_controls.problem: Some links or controls in the page that are identifiable by color (hue) are not visually identifiable via some other means (e.g., underlined, bolded, italicized, sufficient difference in lightness, etc).
color_in_controls.solution: • Check that any text where color is used to convey information is also styled or uses a font that makes it visually distinct from other text around it.

color_in_text.problem: Some text contents in the page use color as the only way to convey information.
color_in_text.solution: • Check that any text where color is used to convey information is also styled or uses a font that makes it visually distinct from other text around it.

input_missing_label.solution:
• Provide descriptive labels for any interactive component within Web content makes the component's purpose clear.
  • Use label elements to associate text labels with form controls. A label is attached to a specific form control through the use of the for attribute. The value of the for attribute must be the same as the value of the id attribute of the form control. The id attribute may have the same value as the name attribute, but both must be provided, and the id must be unique in the Web page.
  • Use WAI-ARIA attributes such as aria-label or aria-labelledby to provide descriptive label without using the label entity.

missing_reflow.solution:
• Content must not be truncated.
  • Use RWD (Responsive Web Design) architecture to allow reflow.

content_on_hover.problem: Content on hover or focus is not perceivable.
content_on_hover.solution:
When an overlay content is present and is appearing after a mouse interaction (e.g. mouse over an element) or a focus event (e.g. focus indicator over an element):

  • Ensure to implement a mechanism allowing the user to close/hide/remove it without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus
  • The pointer can be moved over the additional content without the additional content disappearing
  • The content must persist until the hover or focus is moved out of it, or the widget is deliberately closed or hidden

func_not_operable.problem: Ensure that, wherever possible, content can be operated through a keyboard or keyboard interface. When content can be operated through a keyboard or alternate keyboard, it is operable by people with no vision as well as by people who must use alternate keyboards or input devices that act as keyboard emulators.
func_not_operable.solution: • Ensure that every interactive component or functionality is operable also via keyboard or alternate keyboard.

element_not_focusable.problem: Link or input is not focusable via keyboard.
element_not_focusable.solution: • Use standard HTML form controls and link elements to provide keyboard operation and assistive technology interoperability of interactive user interface elements.

flowSourceType_path.description: Source type; `"url"` = using URL as source and manual settings, `"settings"` = using URL as source and settings from existing *flow*, `"flow"` = continuing from existing *flow*

crawlerSourceType_path.name: sourceType
crawlerSourceType_path.description: Source type; `"url"` = using URL as collection source, `"settings"` = using URL as collection source and settings from existing *flow*, `"flow"` = collecting after existing *flow*

trashedRuns_query.name: trash
trashedRuns_query.description: `false` = return *runs* in "Workspace" and "Archive" folders, `true` return *runs* in "Trash" folder

verificationId_path.name: verificationId
verificationId_path.description: *Keyboard navigation test* ID, in the form "A*n*" (e.g. `"A3703"`)

verificationRunId_path.name: runId
verificationRunId_path.description: *Keyboard navigation test run* ID, in the form "A*n*-n*" (e.g. `"A3687-1747995246599"`)

flowId_path.name: flowId
flowId_path.description: *Flow* (user flow, keyboard flow) ID, in the form "T*n*" (e.g. `"T4143"`)

crawlerId_path.name: crawlerId
crawlerId_path.description: *Crawler* (user flow, keyboard flow) ID, in the form "T*n*" (e.g. `"T4143"`)

changeIndex_query.name: changeIndex
changeIndex_query.description: *Change* index, with `-1` as initial value (no *change* occurred yet), then increasing by 1 for every *change* occurring in the same *step*

issues_manual_query.name: manual
issues_manual_query.description: Include issues that need manual review ("check manually" issue status), along with issues with "need fix" status (included by default)

pagination_page_query.name: page
pagination_page_query.description: Page to display; meaningful only when pagination is activated
